newsitem.title: USA: N. Dakota small grain crop ratings drop on disease.
newsitem.headline: N. Dakota small grain crop ratings drop on disease.

text.p: The following weekly crop report was released by the North Dakota Agricultural Statistics Serivce for the week ended Aug 3.

General: Wet conditions and cool temperatures promoted the development of head and foliar diseases in small grains causing crop condition ratings to drop noticeably, according to the North Dakota Agricultural Statistics Service. Small grain development was mostly ahead of average, despite high disease concerns. Late season crops showed excellent developmental progress for the third consecutive week. Hail damage to crops was reported in northeast, central, east central, and southeast districts. Statewide soil moisture supplies continued to maintain a level comparable with the 5-year average. On average Statewide, there were 7 days suitable for fieldwork during the week ending August 3.

Crops: Small grain development advanced considerably in the turning and beyond stage, well ahead of last year and average. As of August 3, spring wheat was 45 percent in the turning and beyond stage, while durum was at 30 percent turning and beyond, both ahead of average and last year. Combining of durum wheat and barley started with durum slightly ahead average. Harvest of spring wheat and oats were less than 1 percent complete and lagged the 5 year average. Winter wheat harvest was in full swing in the south central district, while other areas have just begun. Late season crops continued to develop at a pace ahead of average and have surpassed last year.

Small grain crop conditions declined last week as continued wet conditions spurred disease development. Spring wheat condition showed the largest decrease. Spring wheat was rated 36 percent good or excellent, compared to 44 percent last week. Durum wheat was rated 34 percent good or excellent, compared to 36 percent last week. Soybean conditions improved considerably due mostly to drier weather in the major growing region while sugarbeets, potatoes, and flaxseed also improved during the week. Conditions of sunflower, corn, dry beans, and canola deteriorated from the previous week. In the east central district, sunflower midge has caused problems in developing heads.
Livestock: Pasture conditions declined from last week and were rated 6 percent very poor, 26 poor, 40 fair, 27 good, and 1 excellent. Hay

condition was rated at 60 percent of normal, unchanged from a week ago. The second cutting of alfalfa was 53 percent complete and other hay was 78 percent. Stockwater supplies were rated 5 percent short, 92 adequate and 3 surplus.

Weather: The past week started off cool as temperatures, especially in the west, were below normal. A persistent stationary front kept clouds over much of the west which did not allow the summer sun to do its work. This front pushed north towards the end of the week allowing temperatures to rebound to more summer-like readings. The highest temperature of 95 degrees was recorded in Edgeley and Bismarck. The lowest temperature of 49 degrees was also recorded in Bismarck and Dazey. Precipitation was light this week with only isolated areas having more than .5 inches. The highest amount recorded was .91 inches in Linton (South Central).

Outlook, August 6 - 12: The week ahead will bring a slow cool down into the weekend as some cool Canadian air sweeps into the state. There will be a chance of showers and thunderstorms in the beginning of the period as the cool air moves into the state. Then a dry weekend with some warming in the beginning of next week.
